modules.text: The Fed held rates at 4.50% for a fifth consecutive meeting.
For the 30 million U.S. households on adjustable-rate mortgages, today's hold extends a 19-month plateau in monthly payments.
The vote came against street consensus, which had priced a 62% probability of a 25-basis-point cut the evening before, per CME FedWatch.
The post-meeting statement removed the prior reference to progress toward the Committee's inflation goal.
We are in no hurry to adjust the stance of policy.
modules.speaker: Jerome Powell

modules.text: Two-year Treasury yields jumped 11 basis points to 4.42% in the hour after the decision.
The next FOMC decision drops June 17; minutes from today's meeting land May 21.
